senses: A person who belays.
A period of a certain number of months.
examples: The drug is known as "seven-monther" – the amount of time it takes to kill.

senses: Spiced with ginger.
A Middle Eastern-style barbecue (cookout), or the barbecue (grill; cooking apparatus) it is cooked on.
ety: Borrowed from Turkish mangal, from Arabic مَنْقَل (manqal).

senses: any device that releases oxygen (or air) into water, especially one in an aquarium
An noncommissioned officer rank in parts of India, later a specific military rank of the British Indian Army and of the modern armies of India and Pakistan, equivalent to sergeant.
ety: Borrowed from Hindustani حوالدار (ḥavāldār) / हविलदार (havildār), from Persian حوالدار (havâldâr), from Arabic حَوَالَة (ḥawāla, “charge”) + Persian دار (dâr, “holder”).

senses: The long fine silky filaments excreted by several mollusks (particularly Pinna nobilis) by which they attach themselves to the sea bed, and from which sea silk is manufactured.
Sea silk manufactured from these filaments.
ety: From Latin byssus, from Ancient Greek βύσσος (bússos, “flax; flax cotton”), from a Semitic source cognate to Hebrew בּוּץ (būṣ, “byssus”) and Aramaic בּוּצָא (būṣā, “byssus”)

senses: A German inn or guesthouse.
A natural hydrate of aluminium, sometimes forming stalactites.
A gemstone consisting of hydrate of aluminium in crystal form.
ety: From Ancient Greek διασπείρω (diaspeírō, “to scatter”), describing its decrepitation on heating.

senses: A kind of central Anatolian rug.
A fan-produced book or magazine of Japanese fiction; especially manga.
ety: Borrowed from Japanese 同(どう)人(じん)誌(し) (dōjinshi, “fan-produced manga or essay booklets”), from 同(どう)人(じん) (dōjin, “group for the same interest”) + 誌(し) (shi, “magazine or a pamphlet”). The spelling is derived from the informal wāpuro rōmaji romanization style of 同人 (どうじん, do-u-ji-n).

senses: An old currency of the Netherlands (and its former overseas territory the Netherlands Antilles or the Dutch East Indies).
ety: From Middle English, from Middle Dutch gulden (florijn) (“golden (florin)”).
examples: The wheel spun and stopped at 13. I had lost! With a feeling like a sick qualm, as though I would like to make my way out of the crowd and go home, I staked another fifty gulden—this time on the red.

senses: Certain cactuses native to the Americas, of genera Selenicereus or Stenocereus, especially the latter.
Fruit of such cactuses, known for its bright skin and speckled flesh.
Providing or designed to provide assistance, especially to persons with a disability
A technician who works with the sound recording and sound effects for films and television.
A native or inhabitant of the south of a region (or of the world as a whole), such as the United Kingdom.
A drink of marc and water.
examples: At dinner Pierre takes a glass of piquette, saying that they had too much wine the day before (the fête day). I look at Charles, and he has piquette too.
She gave him a glass of piquette and a hunch of bread.
With bread for his soup, a bottle of piquette on the table, onions and potatoes, he can carry on.

senses: A piece of music played before a mass; a musical introduction of any sort.
Of or characteristic of grandmothers.
Resembling a grandmother.
examples: One of the maids introduced me to Miss Clifford, the housekeeper, a grandmotherly yet somehow youthful woman who offered me a cup of tea I was too nervous to accept. She gave it to me anyway, calling me “love.”
Then grandmotherly, trust-inspiring 63-year-old Gertrude Pruett stopped sending out the lovely checks and it became harder and harder to get in touch with her or her son Harold.

senses: A fine clay, rich in kaolinite, used in ceramics, papermaking, etc.
ety: From French kaolin, François Xavier d'Entrecolles's irregular romanization of the Mandarin pronunciation of Chinese 高嶺土 /高岭土 (gāolǐngtǔ, “Gaoling earth”), from 高嶺 /高岭 (Gāolǐng, “High Ridge”), a village in Fuliang County, Jingdezhen Prefecture, Jiangxi Province, that became Jingdezhen's primary source of this kind of clay during the early to mid-Qing dynasty.

senses: To clear (a pump) of sediment by starting and stopping it repeatedly.
To beat with a rawhide whip.
A type of sauce made from garlic and olive oil, often with egg and lemon juice and similar to mayonnaise.
ety: Borrowed from French aïoli, from Occitan alhòli, from alh (“garlic”) + òli (“oil”).

senses: Synonym of interpunct ⟨·⟩.
ety: From mid- + dot, possibly as a calque of its alternative name interpunct.

senses: An artificial pool of water ahead of a larger body of water.
The distinctive overhang(s) on a Pennsylvania barn.
ety: From Middle English forbay, equivalent to fore- + bay.

senses: Within a cortex.
A magnifying glass.
A person with an interest in high fidelity music and/or sound reproduction and its associated technology.
Designating a proposed type of marriage (or other partnership) in which the partners plan to have no children and take on no legal obligations to one another.
Friendly, companionable.
Any thorny shrub.
A cocktail of gin, lemon juice, and blackberry liqueur.
ety: From Middle English brembel, from Old English bræmbel, from earlier brǣmel, brēmel, from dialectal Proto-West Germanic *brāmil, diminutive of *brām (English broom).

senses: Impossible to cross.
examples: There is what appears under normal circumstances to be an uncrossable boundary, a total barrier.
There are very few bridges on the footpaths in Skye and even short periods of heavy rain can cause rivers to rise rapidly, often making them uncrossable.

senses: To listen (for example to the heart or lungs) by auscultation; to examine by auscultation.
examples: The doctor, listening past him, had had the same bovine stare as when he was auscultating.

senses: Of animation, erotic, lascivious, lewd, naughty, sexy, suggestive.
ety: From Japanese エッチ (etchi, “dirty; perverted”), which is derived from English aitch (“name of the letter ⟨H⟩”), which is an initialism of the romaji of Japanese 変(へん)態(たい) (hentai, “pervert”). エッチ (etchi) is not a genre in Japanese; this is a development in English (pseudo-Japonism), similar to that of hentai from 変(へん)態(たい) (hentai, “pervert”) above.

senses: remote work, telecommuting, employment as a teleworker.
A fisherman who uses a seine to catch fish.
A fishing vessel used for seining.
A variety of cultivated cherry (Prunus cerasus var. austera), having a dark skin
ety: Probably either: * an alteration of morel with Italian -ello substituted for the ending, perhaps after Italian morello (“dark-coloured”); or * from Italian amarello and/or Dutch amarelle, marelle, both from Medieval Latin amārellum, from Latin amārus + -ellum.

senses: A female adulterer, a married woman or wife who commits adultery.
ety: From adulter (noun) + -ess. In later use typically apprehended as the female equivalent corresponding to adulterer instead.
examples: And the righteous men, they shall iudge them after the manner of adulteresses, and after the manner of women that shed blood; because they are adulteresses, and blood is in their handes.
Do you know what he’s going to endure if he marries a woman the whole community thinks is an adulteress?

senses: A meat substitute resembling turkey, usually made from tofu.
An area of vertical atmospheric rotation in supercell thunderstorms, which signals the threat of a possible tornado.
Without guns.
A line on a graph or chart, such as a weather map, along which all the points have the same temperature.
ety: From the French isotherme (“of equal temperature”, adjective), itself from Ancient Greek ἴσος (ísos, “equal”) + θέρμη (thérmē, “warmth”). By surface analysis, iso- + -therm.
